classification_signals: Abstract: 'This study aims at developing a theoretical framework, a paradigm for noise research and architectural design practice for hospital environments.' (page 3)
Section 1.3: 'the main aim of this study is to develop a theoretical framework for understanding the role and significance of sound perception for improved hospital space experience' (page 10)

Section 1.4: 'A qualitative content analysis was employed to analyse a vast body of literature retrieved' (page 3), 'documentation of studies (including theories of sound perception, empirical studies on sound/noise, evidence-based design theories, and design in architecture as a multisensory medium) was used to address the study objectives.' (page 31)
Chapter 5: 'A MODEL FOR UNDERSTANDING AND IMPROVING HOSPITAL SOUND EXPERIENCE' (page 198)
Figure 1.1: 'A model for understanding the underpinning theories as they relate to sound perception' (page 43)
title: A Model for Understanding the Role of Sound Perception in Hospital Spaces

findings.antecedent: positive aspect of sound in a hospital context
findings.consequent: positive feelings
findings.quote: exploring the positive aspect of sound in a hospital context can evoke positive feelings in both patients and staff.

findings.antecedent: sounds within healthcare soundscapes
findings.consequent: negative impression

findings.antecedent: perception of sound
findings.consequent: positive emotion, stressful health conditions

findings.antecedent: subtler and socially useful understanding of the role of sound and music in the hospital setting
findings.consequent: improved hospital experience for patients and patients care teams
findings.quote: This may create a means for improving the hospital experience for patients and patients care teams.

findings.antecedent: physical environmental factors
findings.consequent: wellness

findings.antecedent: poorly designed environment

findings.antecedent: sound in hospital auditory soundscapes (conveying meaningful information)

findings.antecedent: undesirable sound within the environment of care
findings.consequent: health, recovering process
findings.quote: undesirable sound within the environment of care can evidently be unfavourable to health and impede recovering process

findings.antecedent: poorly planned healthcare design
findings.consequent: psychological and physiological distress
findings.quote: poorly planned healthcare design to psychological and physiological distress

findings.antecedent: hospital spaces (well-designed)
findings.consequent: stress, anxiety, emotional comfort, safety for patients

findings.antecedent: soothing sound of music
findings.consequent: patient attention (distraction from unpleasant to pleasant experience), emotional stress
findings.quote: One feature of such an environment might be soothing sound of music, an intervention that transforms an environment and can help distract patient’s attention away from unpleasant to pleasant experience, thus helping them to deal with emotional stress

findings.antecedent: music

findings.quote: music can facilitate blood pressure recovery from stress

findings.antecedent: certain natural sounds in a given space
findings.consequent: positive feelings
findings.quote: certain natural sounds in a given space may enhance positive feelings

findings.antecedent: positive distraction (soothing sounds of music, fountains, bird song, water bodies) in hospital design
findings.consequent: stress-related outcomes, occupant’s experiences

findings.antecedent: combination of positive distraction therapy and nature sounds

findings.quote: the theory of psychosocially supportive design conceptualised by Dilani’s (2005) affirmed that when a hospital physical environment incorporates water topographies, as well as an orchestra playing pleasant music promotes a positive experience that stimulates the senses, soothes the nerves and makes the whole hospital experience comprehensible, manageable and meaningful.

findings.antecedent: white noise in the intensive care unit
findings.consequent: impact of noise (reduced difference between peak noise and background noise), sleep among patients
findings.quote: Salandin et al. (2011) discovered that implementing white noise in the intensive care unit showed lowered (i.e. reduced difference between peak noise and background noise) impact of noise and improved sleep among patients.

findings.antecedent: music, ocean sounds, random sounds

findings.antecedent: sound (as design factor)

findings.antecedent: auto horns, baby crying, tweeting birds sounds

findings.antecedent: positive influence of sound

findings.antecedent: white noise perception
findings.consequent: mental clarity, relaxation
findings.quote: a study conducted on white noise perception found improved mental clarity and enhanced relaxation in children with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD)

findings.antecedent: viewing sound in the hospital environment as a positive addition to the healthcare soundscape (rather than noise)
findings.consequent: subtler and socially substantive interpretation of the role of sounds in such spaces
findings.quote: viewing sound in the hospital environment as a positive addition to the healthcare soundscape, rather than noise may enable a subtler and socially substantive interpretation of the role of sounds in such spaces.

findings.antecedent: conceptualising sound as soundscape
findings.consequent: health care, ecological quality, psychological benefits, richer positive approach to deal with sound within the hospital context
findings.quote: conceptualising sound in this way would improve the health care, ecological quality, which may promote psychological benefits and would build a richer positive approach to deal with sound within the hospital context.

findings.antecedent: sounds

findings.consequent: hospital experience, health, wellbeing

findings.antecedent: combination of sound design and architectural potentials

This experience includes improved health and wellness, positive feeling/behaviour, space experience acoustic environment satisfaction, speech privacy and intelligibility, reduce isolation and stressful healthcare outcomes.

findings.antecedent: sounds

findings.antecedent: sound

findings.antecedent: pleasant nature sounds (fountains, soft wind, rippling stream, soothing bird songs), comforting music

findings.quote: much of the sound conveys meaningful information that is positive for both occupants, in terms of pleasant nature sounds of fountains, soft wind, rippling stream, soothing bird songs, and comforting music.

findings.antecedent: auditory spatial awareness

findings.quote: when listeners are engaged in auditory spatial awareness, there is that tendency that they can detect and interpret the audible attributes of spatial sound quality.

findings.antecedent: sounds (pleasant/unpleasant)

findings.antecedent: music, ocean sounds, random sounds

findings.antecedent: chirping birds, car horns, babies crying sounds

findings.antecedent: music intervention

findings.antecedent: soothing sound of music

findings.quote: soothing sound of music is an intervention that can help distract patient’s attention away from undesirable experience, thus helping them to deal with emotional stress.

findings.antecedent: hospital physical environment that incorporates orchestra playing pleasant music

findings.antecedent: physical environment in which a patient receives care

findings.quote: the physical environment in which a patient receives care plays a significant role in their outcomes and should reduce pain, anxiety, and stress for patients' comfort and safety.

findings.antecedent: healing comportment of the patient care teams

findings.quote: the healing environment in hospital settings commences with the healing comportment of the patient care teams.

findings.antecedent: secured, trustworthy atmosphere (compassion, clearness, trueness)

findings.antecedent: hospital physical and social environments (designed to reduce stressors: control, social support, nature, positive distractions)

limitations: Insufficient proposed conceptual framework to guide hospital soundscape research (page 19).
Lack of investment in basic scientific research supporting health and economic prosperity of North Cyprus might have undermined the study outcome (page 19).
Rigid governmental policies restricting hospital research, such as not gaining access or obtaining basic information about hospital facilities within North Cyprus (page 19).
Unavailability of enough hospital environments in Gazimağusa, North Cyprus, time constraint, and insufficient income posed major limitations (page 19).
The proposed model is by no means conclusive and could be further expanded for clearer elucidation (page 188).
Many factors affecting sound perception (context, demographics, activity, time and space, preference, sensitivity, visual and hearing impairment) do not relate to the sound itself (page 188).
Due to the diversity of users, the approach may be positioned more for creating patient benefit than for patient care teams (page 188).
minimum_safe_summary: This dissertation develops a theoretical framework for understanding the role of sound perception in hospital spaces, moving beyond the traditional view of sound as merely noise. It synthesizes existing literature from various disciplines, including soundscape design, psychologically supportive design, and psychosocially supportive design, to propose a model for improving hospital experiences. Key findings suggest that incorporating positive sounds (like nature sounds and music) and thoughtful architectural features (like single-patient rooms, natural views, and sound-absorbing materials) can reduce stress, enhance emotional well-being, improve coping strategies, and increase overall satisfaction for patients and staff. The study highlights that sound perception is subjective and influenced by various individual and contextual factors, emphasizing the need for a holistic approach to design. Limitations include the conceptual nature of the model, lack of empirical data from North Cyprus due to research restrictions, and the need for further empirical validation of the proposed concepts.
